title: US WIC participants, Mar 2026
question: USDA Food and Nutrition Service WIC total participants for March 2026, national monthly data, first preliminary print/fixed vintage, not revised values
resolutionSource: USDA Food and Nutrition Service WIC Participation and Costs monthly data, FY 2026 preliminary fixed vintage
resolutionRule: Resolve to the first USDA FNS WIC Participation and Costs national monthly-data print that includes March 2026 total participants, using the published whole-participant count in the Total Participants column. Do not use later revised vintages, FRED, or mirrors; revisions after the first March 2026 print are ignored.
drivers: February 2026 prior-vintage level was below the FY 2025 comparable month
March usually rebounds from February in WIC participation
Recent March observations clustered from roughly 6.62 million to 6.85 million participants
Late-FY2025 and early-FY2026 softness argues against fully matching March 2025
Administrative reporting and state caseload timing can move the first print by tens of thousands

reasoning.result: The prior official vintage states Data as of May 8, 2026 and includes Feb 2026 Total Participants 6,640,819 while not including Mar 2026.

reasoning.call: Fetched official year-earlier and adjacent-month reference points for seasonal and level context.
reasoning.result: Official comparison totals were Feb 2025 6,802,175, Mar 2025 6,850,836, and Apr 2025 6,877,215 participants.

reasoning.call: Checked the official resolution vintage metadata for the first print containing March 2026, using it only for resolver timing and not as forecast evidence.
reasoning.result: The March-inclusive official FNS resolution vintage is dated June 12, 2026 and is the first fetched official vintage after the May 8, 2026 prior vintage; the target row is resolved from that June 12 print.

reasoning.text: Base-rate/reference-class view: a seasonal-naive prior starts from Feb 2026 and adds a typical February-to-March increase. In 2025 the increase was 48,661, while the recent March level range was 6,621,311 to 6,850,836 across 2023-2025.

Model prior: use a simple seasonal persistence model, averaging two anchors: Feb 2026 plus a roughly 45,000 March seasonal rebound, and Mar 2025 adjusted down by the Feb 2026 year-over-year shortfall versus Feb 2025. This intentionally avoids a more complex time-series model because only a small monthly official reference class is needed for this first-print target.

Current-release update: Feb 2026 at 6,640,819 was 161,356 below Feb 2025, so carrying the full year-over-year shortfall to March gives about 6,689,480. A direct Feb-to-Mar seasonal rebound anchor gives about 6,685,000. The point estimate is placed near the midpoint of those pre-release anchors.

Upside scenario: March administrative reporting catches up more than usual, participation retains more of the 2025 level, or state caseload timing adds a larger-than-normal seasonal bounce, putting the first print near or above 6.75 million. Downside scenario: the early-2026 decline persists, the March seasonal bounce is weak, or reporting delays hold the print near 6.60 million.

Point calculation: 0.5 * (6,640,819 + 45,000) + 0.5 * (6,850,836 - 161,356) = 6,687,650, rounded to 6,686,000 after a small downward adjustment for late-2025 and early-2026 softness. The 80% interval is 6,580,000 to 6,795,000, spanning roughly plus 154,000 and minus 106,000 around the point to cover recent first-print seasonal dispersion, reporting timing, and a mildly upside-skewed rebound risk.

Review disposition: Accepted the blocking leakage, update, interval, coherence, and model-prior critiques by removing the realized March 2026 value from evidence and historicalContext, widening the interval to ex-ante forecast uncertainty, and adding a seasonal-persistence prior. Kept the official resolver metadata and June 12 resolution source only for resolution clarity.
